countries.title: What people pay for a dollar in {count} countries, against the official rate
countries.lede: The official rate is the one banks and governments quote. We compare it with what people actually pay each other for a dollar, every hour.
countries.loadFailed: Could not load this hour's prices. Try again in a few minutes.
countries.metaTemplate: Checked {time} UTC. {n} of {total} countries have a price this hour. Prices come from offers to sell stablecoins, digital tokens worth one dollar, on markets where people trade directly with each other. Each price is the middle of the last 24 hours of readings, so one odd reading cannot move it.
countries.bigTitleEmpty: No country has a large gap this hour
countries.modTitleTemplate: {n} more {countries} where people pay {min}% to {max}% more
countries.modTitleEmpty: No more countries have a large gap this hour
countries.emptyGroup: No country in this group has a gap this hour.
countries.pegTitle: Currencies fixed to the dollar or euro
countries.pegNote: These currencies hold their official rate, so paying more is the cost of getting hold of a digital dollar, not a currency losing value. A digital dollar is a stablecoin, a token meant to stay worth one dollar. Fixed means the government holds its currency at a set rate. Here that means the CFA franc, one currency shared by several countries in Africa, fixed to the euro. It also means the Gulf currencies, each fixed to the dollar.
countries.nearTitleTemplate: {n} {countries} where people pay the official rate, give or take {gap}%
countries.nearNote: A plus sign means people pay more than the official rate and a minus sign means less.
countries.withheldNoteTemplate: We only publish a price when at least {min} people are selling. Fewer than that is not a market, so we say so instead of guessing.
countries.cfaNote: Each CFA entry is a currency shared by several countries. We count it once, as one price.
countries.depthNoteTemplate: "How much you could buy" is how many dollars are on offer near that price. A price with almost no money behind it is not really a price. A plus sign means at least that much, because we stop counting there. A gap is how much more people pay than the official rate. The small figure under each Gap now is how much that gap moved since the Gap on date, in percentage points. A note beside a country code says why that price is less certain. Buy and sell prices far apart means sellers ask much more than buyers offer, so we still show the price but trust it less.
countries.reasonFarApart: buy and sell prices far apart

withheldReasons.nobody is offering to sell dollars here: no one is selling dollars right now
withheldReasons.the buying and selling sides are not the: buy and sell prices far apart, so there is no single price

countries.frozenOneTemplate: {names} has a price but is not ranked, because its official rate is frozen. A frozen rate is one the government has stopped updating, so comparing to it measures the freeze, not what people pay.
countries.frozenManyTemplate: {names} have a price but are not ranked, because their official rates are frozen. A frozen rate is one the government has stopped updating, so comparing to it measures the freeze, not what people pay.
